entities.summary:
Dai Jin (unknown - 1462) was a prominent leader in the early Ming Revival of the Ma-Xia, or the Zhe School style of landscape painting. This artistic movement emerged during the late Southern Song dynasty and emphasized the importance of natural scenery and subtle human emotions. Dai Jin's innovative compositions not only contributed to the development of this unique aesthetic but also influenced a new generation of artists.

His leadership was instrumental in shaping the cultural identity of the Ming dynasty, which would go on to have a profound impact on Chinese art, literature, and politics.

The Zhe School's emphasis on natural beauty and human subtlety resonated with the societal values of the time, reflecting the changing attitudes towards nature, society, and individualism in Ming China.

Today, Dai Jin is remembered as a key figure in the evolution of Chinese landscape painting, whose legacy continues to inspire artists and art historians alike.
